title: Gun position before the target appears
summary: In Sporting™ the stock stays below a line on the vest until the target appears. In Compak® Sporting the gun position at the call is free.

body.html: At a Parcours de Chasse – Sporting™ competition, shooters call for the target with the gun held low. This is a rule, not a matter of style. Compak® Sporting has no such rule.
In Sporting™ the stock stays below the line on the vest until the target appears; calling with the gun already up brings a warning and a yellow card the first time.
body.heading: Watch the gun position

html.sporting: Gun low: the top back of the stock is kept under the vest line until you see the target.
html.compak: Free: the gun may already be at the shoulder, or lower. There is no line on the vest, but the shot is still fired from the shoulder.

body.html: In Sporting™, before you call, both your feet are inside the stand. The heel of the stock (its top back corner, the part that goes into your shoulder) touches your body. The highest back point of the stock, usually the heel itself, stays below the line on the vest. You keep this ready position until the target has left the trap and you can see it.

The line is marked on the vest or jacket 25 cm below the shoulder axis (an imaginary horizontal line through both shoulders), parallel to it. Its colour stands out against the vest, so the referee can see it. The rule covers all kinds of stock: standard, Monte Carlo (with a raised comb, the top edge of the stock where your cheek rests) and adjustable comb.
You may bring the gun up to your shoulder (mount it) only once the target appears. All targets, the rabbit too, are shot with the gun at the shoulder; shooting from the hip is not allowed.
One relaxation: in a double, you may hold the gun as you like between the first and the second target. Before the first target the low position still applies.

Penalties: the first time you call in a wrong position or mount the gun too early, the referee gives a spoken warning and shows a yellow card. Doing it again on the same layout costs a red card: a single is scored zero, and doubles follow the table in the rules guide (Chapter 12 · Red card on repeat at the same layout).

Mounting the gun and swinging it along the line where you expect the target, before you call, is mock shooting, and it is forbidden too. The first time brings a warning. If it happens again, the next target you hit is scored zero.
If you shoot both disciplines, many coaches suggest training the low-gun start before a Sporting™ event, even if you call gun-up in Compak® Sporting.

notes.html: If a coach drills a gun-up start before a Sporting™ event, make sure the word 'drill' is translated too: it is an exercise, not the competition start.

key_points.html: Sporting™: before the call, both feet in the stand, the heel of the stock (its top back corner) on your body and below the vest line.
Sporting™: the vest line is 25 cm below the shoulder axis (a line through both shoulders), in a contrasting colour.
Sporting™: mount only when the target appears; the gun position is free only between the two targets of a double.
Sporting™: the first offence brings a warning with a yellow card, the next one on the same layout a red card.
Compak® Sporting: the position at the call is free and there is no vest line; the shot is still fired from the shoulder.

did_you_know.html: The low-gun start is often explained by the hunting roots of Sporting™: a hunter rarely waits for a bird with the gun already at the shoulder.

quiz.q: How far below the shoulder axis (an imaginary line through both shoulders) is the vest line in Sporting™?
quiz.explain: The line runs 25 cm below the shoulder axis, parallel to it.

quiz.q: May you call for the target in Compak® Sporting with the gun already at the shoulder?

options.text: No, the gun must start low

quiz.explain: Compak® Sporting has no low-gun rule and no vest line; only the shot itself must be fired from the shoulder.

quiz.q: When may you hold the gun as you like in Sporting™?

options.text: Between the two targets of a double
Before the first target of a double

quiz.explain: The free position is allowed only between the two targets of a double; before the first one the ready position applies.
